title: libparted-fs-resize0-3.8-1.1 on GA media
description: A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in parted when processing specially crafted FAT32 filesystem images due to an integer calculation error during buffer allocation. A local attacker could exploit this by tricking a user or automated service into opening a malicious filesystem image, potentially causing an application crash resulting in denial of service or memory corruption.
aiSummary: The vulnerability in parted involves a heap-based buffer overflow triggered by an integer calculation error during buffer allocation when handling a malicious FAT32 filesystem image. This flaw allows a local attacker to cause an application crash or potentially corrupt memory by enticing a user or automated process to open a crafted filesystem image.
aiImpact: Exploitation can lead to denial of service through application crashes or potential memory corruption, which may affect the stability or security of the affected system. There is no indication of remote exploitation or active exploits in the wild.
